title: Latency/Quality Pareto-frontier evaluation for batching and KV-cache config matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a reproducible Pareto-frontier analysis that maps batching and KV-cache configuration combinations to latency (p50/p95) and generation quality (task-level correctness and hallucination rate) across representative workloads. Background: recent config sweeps have reduced cost but caused subtle quality regressions on long-prefix chat flows and reranking routes. This ticket ties together a structured evaluation harness, new metrics, and monitoring hooks so we can (1) quantify tradeoffs, (2) publish safe default config sets per route, and (3) wire regression detection into the CI/monitoring pipeline.

Scope and focus:
- Systematically sweep microbatch sizes, continuous-batch thresholds, prefix-KV cache TTLs, and cache-granularity (per-session vs per-route).
- Measure latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), token-level throughput, and quality metrics: ROUGE/EM-style exact-match where appropriate, embedding-similarity to reference outputs, and a lightweight hallucination classifier score from the eval harness.
- Include interaction variables: quantization level (int8/16), model-variant fallback, and sequence-length distribution.
- Target workloads: chat long-prefix (20–1024 prefix tokens), streaming generation (low-latency SLOs), embeddings-heavy reranking routes.
- Deliverables: reproducible notebooks + CI job, dashboards with Pareto front visualizations, config recommendation doc, and a staged canary in staging cluster.

Methodology:
1) Build a matrix generator that emits config combinations prioritized by expected SLO risk (we weight high-impact dimensions like prefix TTL more).
2) Run mini-benchmarks on dedicated staging pool and collect traces + token-level timings. Use synthetic traces derived from production histograms plus a small holdout of real anonymized requests.
3) Compute per-config quality metrics using the eval harness (reference prompts, human-labeled subset for hallucination). For speed, use stratified sampling and a tuned early-stop when quality is clearly off the Pareto frontier.
4) Produce Pareto frontier plots and a shortlist of candidate configs that trade <=10% latency improvement for <=1% quality delta (configurable).
5) Wire selected configs into the regression monitor: baseline vs candidate diff alerts, auto-fallback on quality regression, and post-deploy smoke checks.

Why this is different from prior work:
- Prior sweeps focused on sensitivity; this is explicitly building the Pareto frontier artifacts and operationalizing them into monitoring and rollout gates.
- We introduce token-level SNR (signal-to-noise) and a compact hallucination signal to make quality deltas easier to detect in CI.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: sampling bias from synthetic traces. Mitigation: include a small real request holdout and run a sanity check on production shadow traffic before canary rollback.
- Risk: noisy quality signals when deltas are tiny. Mitigation: aggregate across multiple prompt families, use embedding-similarity thresholds, and require consistency across metrics before gating.

- Run full sweep on staging pool (expected ~24h compute) and produce draft dashboard by 2026-03-16.

updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with RM, Product, and Reliability. Agreed on target SLO bands and the initial readability metrics to use (embedding-similarity + hallucination classifier).

2026-02-25: Prototype matrix generator implemented; initial 48-config sweep run on a small staging pool. Early result: microbatch=4 + TTL=60s reduces p50 by 12% but shows a 1.8% drop in task-EM on long-prefix chat prompts.

2026-03-01: Determined signal amplification from quantization at int8 is confounded with cache TTL. Decided to treat quantization as an orthogonal axis and run separate short-circuit checks rather than full cross-product to save compute.
2026-03-07: PR opened for CI harness and lightweight hallucination classifier (runtime repo PR #6842). Requesting review from @Jingwen Li and @Ethan Morales.
2026-03-10: Experiment run in progress on staging (24h). Initial dashboards populating. Next sync scheduled 2026-03-11 to review early Pareto curves and pick candidate configs for canary.
